peg.peg_mechanism_score_basis: MEASURES THE MECHANISM'S DESIGN AND ITS TRACK RECORD, NOT THE CURRENT −42bp DEVIATION. USG runs the crvUSD architecture, which is proven, and has held WITHOUT POL ISSUANCE AND WITHOUT BAD DEBT — both of which are the failure modes this design is usually docked for. ⚠️ THE SCORE IS CAPPED AT 5.0 NOT ON MECHANISM QUALITY BUT ON SCALE: an architecture proven at crvUSD's size is being run on a ~$5.8M book, and a mechanism's track record does not transfer across two orders of magnitude of depth.

backing.backing_score_basis: ✅ MEASURES ACTUAL OVERCOLLATERALIZATION, AND UNLIKE MOST OF THIS CORPUS THE RATIO IS A REAL MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN AN IDENTITY. Borrower collateral ~$4.81M against ~$3.76M debt = ~128% CR; the feed reads collateral_ratio 129.02 on total_backing $5,758,937.73 with a surplus of $1,295,336.95. ✅ THESE ARE INDEPENDENT QUANTITIES — collateral posted by borrowers is not defined as equal to debt issued — so the ~129% CARRIES INFORMATION, which cannot be said of the 100.0 ratios on wrapper and PSM-style assets. POL debt $0 and bad debt $0. ⚠️ HELD AT 5.0 DESPITE A GENUINELY SOUND RATIO because the axis prices the COLLATERAL and the ORACLE behind it, not the arithmetic: this is a small book of borrower positions marked by oracle-NAV, and a 129% ratio on illiquid collateral is not equivalent to 129% on cash.
backing.backing_score_persistence: filtered — collateral composition, though the ratio itself is spot-responsive
backing.backing_score_denominator: ✅ ASK WHAT THE RATIO DIVIDES BY — and here the answer is the good one: borrower collateral over borrower debt, two independently determined quantities. Contrast usdat, susds and the syrup pools, where backing is DEFINED as the supply and the ratio is an accounting identity.

liquidity.liquidity_score_basis: ⚠️ CUT 3.5 → 3.0 ON 2026-10-16: ALL THREE SUB-METRICS DETERIORATED AND THE EXIT IS NOW MEASURED. Counter-side inventory in the two keeper pools is $887,947 (USDC $398,088 + frxUSD $489,860), DOWN 21% from ~$1.13M on 2026-08-05 and from ~$1.28M on 2026-06-10 — a two-step adverse trend, not a single read. Both pools are MORE USG-heavy than before, 72.91% and 70.81% against ~69% on both in August, which is the mechanical signature of a discount the mechanism cannot correct. Keeper defense capacity is $0 because debt() = 0 on both keepers, so none of that inventory is protocol-controlled. ⚠️ MEASURED get_dy LADDER (riskAnalyst, Ethereum block 26,202,522, fees in, gas out): USDC pool costs 0.51% at 10K USG, 0.68% at 100K, 1.36% at 250K, then 21.8% at 500K; frxUSD pool 0.43% / 0.54% / 0.90%, then 7.5% at 500K and 51.2% at 1M. SO ROUGHLY $500K — ABOUT 13% OF THE $3,823,946 SUPPLY — LEAVES AT ≤1.4% ACROSS BOTH POOLS, AND ESSENTIALLY NOTHING BEYOND IT. ⚠️ AND sUSG HOLDS A FURTHER 33.0% OF SUPPLY (1,262,646 USG) THAT WOULD HAVE TO TRANSIT THESE SAME TWO POOLS TO REACH DOLLARS. No CEX backstop. ⚠️ THIS IS THE AXIS TO READ FIRST ON THIS ASSET: backing is genuinely sound at 129.65% CR with zero bad debt, and a reader who stops there will conclude USG is well-positioned. Collateral adequacy and exit capacity are different questions, and only one of them is comfortable here.
liquidity.liquidity_score_persistence: filtered — keeper inventory, pool imbalance and venue structure, not spot depth. Re-check on a further fall in counter-side stables, either pool crossing 75% USG, or the measured 250K rung exceeding ~2%.
liquidity.liquidity_score_depth_caveat: The feed computes a ladder for this asset; this score additionally carries riskAnalyst's own get_dy measurement on both keeper pools, quoted in the basis with its block. Quotes are read-only route estimates including pool fees and excluding gas — they are not executed fills. (Supersedes the 2026-09-11 note that the feed computed no depth at all, and the pre-ladder inventory-only framing.)
liquidity.liquidity_score_band_divergence: ⚠️⚠️ A DASHBOARD BAND AND THIS SCORE MEASURE DIFFERENT THINGS AND NEITHER IS WRONG. The band measures the SIZE OF THE 2% CROSSING RELATIVE TO SUPPLY, which is a defensible and more favourable question for a book this small. THIS SCORE MEASURES THE FRAGILITY OF THE SOURCE: one mechanism's declining, increasingly imbalanced, non-protocol-controlled inventory is the whole exit. ⚠️⚠️ AND THE SLOPE SUPPORTS THE LOWER NUMBER — on the measured ladder the USDC pool goes from 1.36% at 250K to 21.8% at 500K, a 16× cost increase across a 2× size increase. That is a cliff immediately above the crossing, not a gentle degradation, and a 2%-crossing figure cannot express it: the band reports WHERE the curve crosses 2%, not HOW STEEPLY it leaves.
liquidity.liquidity_score_ladder: ⚠️⚠️ REVISED 2026-09-12, AND THE LADDER IS WORSE THAN THE SUPPLY FRAME MADE IT LOOK. MEASURED EXIT COST BY SIZE (even split across every PegKeeper pool): $10,000 → −50.4bps · $50,000 → −52.6bps · $100,000 → −55.7bps · $250,000 → −67.1bps · $500,000 → −99.6bps · $750,000 → −187.0bps · $1,000,000 → −657.3bps. ⚠️⚠️ IT COSTS FIFTY BASIS POINTS TO EXIT TEN THOUSAND DOLLARS. That is the smallest rung measured, and it is already expensive — this asset is costly at RETAIL size, not merely at scale. ⚠️ The curve then bends hard: ~100bps at half a million, ~187bps at $750k, and 657bps at $1M. 2% crossing BRACKETED $750,000–$1,000,000. ⚠️ THE EARLIER BASIS LED ON '~16.8% of supply exits at 2%' AND ON KEEPER INVENTORY AS A SHARE OF THE BOOK. Withdrawn as the measure: a holder does not care what fraction of supply clears, they care that their $10k costs 50bps. ✅ THE COUNTER-SIDE FIGURE IS STILL THE RIGHT SECOND INSTRUMENT and is kept: sell_side_counter_inventory_usd $1,049,612.88 — 'what a USG seller can actually execute into', which is why the ladder dies just past $1M. ⚠️ AND keeper_defense_capacity IS EXCLUDED BY THE PRODUCER as 'peg-defense capability, not observed market depth' — not re-imported here.

dependencies.underlying_score_basis: MEASURES THE COUNTERPARTY SET BEHIND THE LOAN BOOK. ⚠️ AUTHORED 2026-09-06 — PREVIOUSLY UNSCORED, and it is arguably USG's MOST LOAD-BEARING AXIS, because what backs USG is a book of borrower positions and the quality of that book is a dependency question rather than a ratio question. A 129% CR describes the arithmetic; this axis describes what is inside it.
